page: Microsoft Azure DC16es_v6 is a general-purpose confidential computing virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built upon the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon TDX processor offering 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The CPU operates at clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz and integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a substantial 260 MB shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction extensions are available, including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The configuration includes 64.0 GB of system RAM, providing an even 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation that aligns with general-purpose workload profiles. Local ephemeral storage is absent on this server type, requiring attached Azure premium storage volumes for persistent file systems and operating system installations. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its compute resources entirely toward CPU-centric enterprise execution environments.

Benchmark metrics reflect balanced processing capabilities with pronounced single-thread strength. The DC16es_v6 achieves strong single-core scores in Geekbench, reaching 1944.0 points, while multi-core workloads yield average scores of 11137.0 in Geekbench and 14092.2 in stress-ng. PassMark tests confirm steady mid-tier computation with a CPU score of 23118.53, alongside 18.44 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, PassMark memory performance is comparatively weak in bottom-quartile percentiles, presenting a potential throughput bottleneck for memory-bus-intensive applications.

With dedicated high-clock cores, robust cache density, and AMX support, the DC16es_v6 delivers practical qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound transactional systems without requiring GPU overhead. It is appropriately deployed for confidential cloud computing, application server tiers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web backends, and moderate in-memory key-value stores.
description: Microsoft Azure DC16es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for compute and memory-balanced enterprise workloads. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon TDX processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores operating at up to 4.2 GHz, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It provides 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512, AMX matrix acceleration, and hardware cryptographic instruction sets such as AES and VAES. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, relying instead on remote premium storage attachments, and contains no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core Geekbench performance alongside average multi-core and database operational throughput, though memory subtests register lower relative efficiency. The DC16es_v6 is suitable for enterprise general-purpose processing, confidential computing tasks, software compilation, and in-memory caching platforms such as Redis.
